info.dotcraftjei.drain.1: Creative-only test block: takes any amount of FE from any side and destroys it, and pulls FE out of every neighbour on all sides. It cannot be crafted, is unbreakable in survival and drops nothing.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.1: A turbine pod that only runs while it is waterlogged: place it in water or use a water bucket on it. It is sealed, so it holds water but never spreads it. Without water it makes nothing and has a chance to explode (small blast, no block damage) every 30 ticks.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.2: Best placement: deep in an ocean or river, in a body of water with a current. Another flow generator next to it does not count as water.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.3: Peak without animals, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s FE/t. Buffer: %2$s FE.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.4: It counts the water in the 3x3x3 cube around it: a source block counts %2$s, flowing water %3$s. The water share is full at a weight of %1$s (tiers 1 to 5); more water does not help.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.5: The flow axis (front and back of the pod) must stay free for the water: a solid block there makes the output 0. FE leaves through the other four sides only.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.6: Fauna bonus: every different kind of animal swimming nearby (up to %1$s kinds) adds %2$s, so up to +%3$s on top of the peak. The search radius is %4$s blocks (tier 1: %5$s).
info.dotcraftjei.flow.7: Biome: outside ocean and river biomes the output is %1$s (from tier 3 on %2$s); tier 5 does not care about the biome.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.perk.1: Baseline: needs a nearly full cube of water.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.perk.2: Wide net: animals count within a larger radius, and less water is needed.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.perk.3: Adaptation: keeps a bigger share of the output outside ocean and river.
info.dotcraftjei.flow.perk.4: Lean water: a small pond is already enough.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.1: A winch that flies a kite on a tether. The kite catches the wind and the winch turns it into FE. Put the kite in with a right-click; sneak with an empty hand to take it back.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.2: Best placement: open ground with a free sky above the winch, and at least %1$s blocks from every other kite generator.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.3: Iron wire is the tether: right-click the winch with iron wire, 1 wire = 1 block of tether, at most (tiers 1 to 5) %1$s blocks. Without wire no kite flies.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.4: Base, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s FE/t. Output = base x length factor (effective length / %2$s) x free air x weather x wind: the longer the tether, the more FE.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.5: Tiers 4 and 5 fly two kites that share the base and wander +-%1$s blocks around the vertical axis of the winch, at least 3 blocks apart.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.6: Minimum distance: two kite generators with a kite and wire that are closer than %1$s blocks tangle, and both stay down (too close) until one is removed or moved away.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.7: Storms: tiers 1 to 3 reel the kite in during a thunderstorm, tier 4 flies at half output, tier 5 ignores thunder. In a storm the kite stays within %1$s blocks of the axis, and lightning within %1$s blocks is drawn to it, rarely: %2$s FE per bolt (tiers 4 and 5).
info.dotcraftjei.kite.perk.1: Plain kite: needs a free 3x3 way up, rain halves the output.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.perk.2: Waxed line: rain costs only a quarter.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.perk.3: Rain-proof sail that ignores obstructions: blocks above and a crowded sky cost nothing.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.perk.4: Storm line: flies in a thunderstorm at half output, a crowded sky costs half as much, two kites.
info.dotcraftjei.kite.perk.5: Insulated tether: ignores thunder and a crowded sky, two kites.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.1: Turns moonlight into FE. It follows the height of the moon, which is always opposite to the sun, so it works at night and never at the same time as a solar panel. It makes nothing under cover or in a dimension without a sky.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.2: Best placement: open sky above it, kept dark. Block light above it (light pollution) takes up to half of the output. Moon-friendly biomes multiply the output by %1$s, unfriendly ones by %2$s.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.3: Peak at full moon in a clear night, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s FE/t. Buffer: %2$s FE.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.4: Share of the full moon output that is left at new moon, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.5: Share of the output that stays in rain, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s. A thunderstorm halves what rain leaves.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.6: Panels (solar and lunar, any tier) that touch each other sideways in one plane share one pool of FE, up to %1$s panels: the buffers add up and a neighbour draws from the whole pool.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.7: A waterlogged panel makes only %1$s of its output. A living entity standing on the panel shades it: it makes nothing while the entity is there.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.perk.1: Baseline panel; rain hurts a lot, new moon is weak.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.perk.2: Copes better with rain; stronger at new moon.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.perk.3: Moon tracking: a wider plateau around midnight, and rain costs less.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.perk.4: Better moon tracking and little loss in rain.
info.dotcraftjei.lunar.perk.5: Best moon tracking; immune to rain; half of the output even at new moon.
info.dotcraftjei.melt.1: Burns ice for FE. A heat source (lava, fire, magma, a lit campfire or furnace) must touch it; every pulse it melts ice, packed ice or blue ice that touches its other sides into air.
info.dotcraftjei.melt.2: Best placement: between a heat source and a stack of ice, next to a battery. Heat is not used up, ice is the only running cost; a melted block is gone.
info.dotcraftjei.melt.3: A melted block gives %1$s FE (ice), %2$s FE (packed ice) or %3$s FE (blue ice). The FE go into a heat reservoir that releases at most the peak per tick, tiers 1 to 5: %4$s FE/t.
info.dotcraftjei.melt.4: Tiers 4 and 5 keep the water of the melted ice in a tank of %1$s buckets that can only be drained. While it is full every melted block gives only %2$s of its FE: drain it.
info.dotcraftjei.melt.perk.4: Water recovery: one bucket per melted block goes into the tank.
info.dotcraftjei.melt.perk.5: Five blocks, four times a second, and all the water comes back: a melted block gives as many buckets as it is worth ice.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.1: Turns sunlight into FE. It follows the height of the sun, so it makes nothing at night, under cover or in a dimension without a sky.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.2: Best placement: open sky above it, for example on a roof or a field. Sun-friendly biomes multiply the output by %1$s, unfriendly ones by %2$s.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.3: Peak at noon under a clear sky, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s FE/t. Buffer: %2$s FE.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.4: Share of the output that stays in rain, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s. A thunderstorm halves what rain leaves.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.5: Panels (solar and lunar, any tier) that touch each other sideways in one plane share one pool of FE, up to %1$s panels: the buffers add up and a neighbour draws from the whole pool.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.6: A waterlogged panel makes only %1$s of its output. A living entity standing on the panel shades it: it makes nothing while the entity is there.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.perk.1: Baseline panel; rain hurts a lot.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.perk.3: Sun tracking: a wider plateau around noon, and rain costs less.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.perk.4: Better sun tracking and little loss in rain.
info.dotcraftjei.solar.perk.5: Best sun tracking; immune to rain.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.1: Makes FE from the temperature difference between a hot and a cold neighbour, day and night and in every dimension.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.2: Best placement: a heat source on one face and a cold source on the opposite face (heat: lit furnace, campfire, fire, magma, lava; cold: water, snow, ice, packed ice, blue ice). Only opposite faces count; with only a hot or only a cold side it makes nothing.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.3: Heat and cold have levels 1 to %1$s each; both together give a difference of %2$s to %3$s. The best of the three axes counts, axes do not add up.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.4: Peak, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s FE/t, reached at a temperature difference of %2$s.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.5: More sources of the same kind do not add up, and nothing is consumed: a lava bucket and a block of ice last forever.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.perk.2: Baseline efficiency at a higher peak.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.perk.3: Efficiency: the full peak needs a smaller difference.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.perk.4: Efficiency of tier 3 at a higher peak.
info.dotcraftjei.thermo.perk.5: Best efficiency: for example magma and ice already give the full peak.
info.dotcraftjei.vibration.1: Listens to the shocks of the world like a sculk sensor: blocks broken and placed, explosions, deaths, damage, lightning, landings and steps (what it hears depends on the tier). A louder event gives more FE.
info.dotcraftjei.vibration.2: Best placement: where things happen, next to a mine, a mob farm or an arena. Sneaking players and spectators are not heard, and wool between the event and the generator stops the vibration up to tier 3.
info.dotcraftjei.vibration.3: Peak (burst power), tiers 1 to 5: %1$s FE/t. On average it makes at most this share of the peak: %2$s.
info.dotcraftjei.vibration.4: Hearing radius, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s blocks. Quietest vibration frequency it hears: %2$s (lower is fainter).
info.dotcraftjei.vibration.5: Boss bonus: game events caused by a boss (by default ender dragon, wither, warden, elder guardian; the list is configurable) are worth %1$s times as much, at every tier.
info.dotcraftjei.vibration.6: Hard cap: a bucket that holds %1$s ticks of peak and refills slowly, so a looping machine (grinder, dispenser, mob pen) cannot make more than the average above.
info.dotcraftjei.vibration.perk.1: Hears the loud shocks: blocks, deaths, explosions, lightning.
info.dotcraftjei.vibration.perk.5: Also hears steps, and has the largest radius.
info.dotcraftjei.wheel.1: A mob that runs on the wheel turns it. One mob on the wheel is held in place and keeps running; babies, mobs in water, mounted mobs and pets told to sit do not count, bosses and the mobs in the config list wheel.blocked_mobs are never captured, and one wheel holds one animal.
info.dotcraftjei.wheel.2: Best placement: a wheel in a pen next to a battery. The pull of the mob, its weight, comes from its health and its speed; a mob that only stands counts half.
info.dotcraftjei.wheel.3: Peak with a strong runner, tiers 1 to 5: %1$s FE/t.
